section: Kakatiya society and religion - Veerashaivism, Jainism, temple institutions

accepted.s: Royal women during the Kakatiya period were active donors primarily to which of the following?
o: Guild halls and royal mint houses
accepted.x: Royal women of the Kakatiya period made donations to temples and tanks, contributing to both religious institutions and public water works.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise institutional pair instead of being distracted by other public and religious establishments.

accepted.s: Who among the following was the queen of Prataparudra II associated with royal donations to temples and tanks?
accepted.x: Lakshmidevi, the queen of Prataparudra II, is cited as an example of a royal woman who donated to temples and tanks.
accepted.tq: Match the royal person with the specific deed and avoid substituting other prominent Kakatiya women.

accepted.s: Kuppamamba and Mailama are associated with which aspect of Kakatiya history?
o: The legal regulation of religious endowments
The dynastic deity of the Kakatiyas
accepted.x: Kuppamamba and Mailama are associated with the subject of royal women's grants in the Kakatiya period.
accepted.tq: Use the heading-level association to distinguish royal grants from religious and legal themes.

accepted.s: The Kakatiya age is often characterised as the:
accepted.x: The Kakatiya age is called the Shaiva era because Shaivism had a prominent position during the period.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the period-label relationship without confusing the presence of other religious traditions with the dominant characterisation.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the dynastic deity of the Kakatiyas?
accepted.x: Svayambhu Shiva was the dynastic deity of the Kakatiyas.
accepted.tq: Test the exact deity associated with the ruling dynasty rather than a prominent regional shrine.

accepted.s: In the dispute concerning Sri Swamy Hathiramji Mutt at Tirupati, the courts clarified the power of the State regarding interim management of old religious endowments under which legal framework?
o: The AP Endowments Act, 1987 and Articles 25–26 of the Constitution
The AP Endowments Act, 1966 and Articles 14–15 of the Constitution
The AP Charitable Trusts Act, 1990 and Articles 36–39 of the Constitution
The Religious Institutions Act, 1987 and Articles 32–35 of the Constitution
accepted.x: The legal framework comprises the AP Endowments Act, 1987 and Articles 25 and 26 of the Constitution, in relation to State powers over interim management of old religious endowments.
accepted.tq: Identify the competent legal framework by combining the relevant statute with the constitutional provisions on religious freedom and denominational affairs.

accepted.s: Which of the following groups correctly represents the Shaiva-Shakta axis of Andhra that continued through the Kakatiya period?
accepted.x: Srisailam, Alampur and Draksharama remained important centres of the Shaiva-Shakta axis of Andhra during the period.
accepted.tq: Use the geographic cluster as a group and eliminate combinations drawn from unrelated regional or dynastic centres.
